title: 2017 AMC 12B Problem 4
statement: Samia set off on her bicycle to visit her friend, traveling at an average speed of \(17\) kilometers per hour. When she had gone half the distance to her friend’s house, a tire went flat, and she walked the rest of the way at \(5\) kilometers per hour. In all it took her \(44\) minutes to reach her friend’s house. In kilometers rounded to the nearest tenth, how far did Samia walk?

solutions.text:
Let \(2d\) be the total distance, so she biked \(d\) at \(17\) km/h and walked \(d\) at \(5\) km/h. The total time in hours is \[\frac{d}{17} + \frac{d}{5} = \frac{44}{60}.\] Combining the left side gives \(\dfrac{22d}{85} = \dfrac{11}{15},\) so \(d = \dfrac{11}{15} \cdot \dfrac{85}{22} = \dfrac{17}{6} = 2.833\ldots\) She walked about \(2.8\) kilometers.

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Let \(d\) be the one-way distance she biked (and also walked); use time \(= \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{rate}}\)
